title: GH-5: Compare two generation runs for reproducibility
description:
We need a way to compare two generation runs side-by-side to evaluate reproducibility. The workflow is:

1. Start a generation run and execute measure.
2. Stop the generation.
3. Repeat steps 1-2 for a second run.
4. Compare the outputs stored in history/.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Compare the two runs and determine whether the prompts are identical across runs.
- Compare the two runs and determine whether the beads issues are identical across runs.
- Analyze differences in results between the two runs.
- Report on what factors contribute to divergence and what can be done to make them more similar.

GitHub: petar-djukic/go-unix-utils#5

title: Run generation A: start, measure, stop
description:
Run the first generation cycle to produce baseline history outputs.

Steps:
1. Commit any pending changes (clean working tree required by generator)
2. mage generator:start
3. mage cobbler:measure
4. mage generator:stop
5. Verify history/ contains measure output files (prompt, issues, log, stats)

The history files from this run are labeled by timestamp and serve as Run A.

title: Run generation B: start, measure, stop
description:
Run the second generation cycle to produce comparison history outputs.

Steps:
1. mage generator:start
2. mage cobbler:measure
3. mage generator:stop
4. Verify history/ now contains outputs from both Run A and Run B

The history files from this run are labeled by a later timestamp and serve as Run B.

title: Semantic comparison of Run A vs Run B using Claude
description:
Semantically compare the two generation runs using Claude as the comparator.

Compare:
1. Prompts: Are the measure prompts from Run A and Run B semantically equivalent?
2. Issues: Are the proposed beads issues equivalent in scope, structure, and intent?
3. Stats: How do token usage and timing compare?

Analysis:
- Identify sources of non-determinism
- Report on what can be done to improve reproducibility
- Write findings as a summary

The comparison must be semantic (not byte-for-byte) since LLM outputs vary even at temperature 0.
